correctness.rationale: The integer two-torus kernel theorem is applied to A^n−J^n. Cayley–Hamilton gives the skew-difference recurrence and determinant exact even/odd formulas; positivity U_3≥8 leaves precisely the n=1,δ=−2 non-tame exception and n=1,δ=−1 absolute-value correction. Summing parity-selected generating series gives both zeta formulas; their local logarithmic derivative has residue 1−i·sgn(δ) at i in the nonsymmetric tame case, impossible for an algebraic Puiseux germ, while the symmetric square root has simple uncanceled zeros. Eigenvalue dominance proves root-growth statements. Independent integer matrix and formal rational-series computations in verify.py passed for 11 matrices through n=32; finiteness of this test is explicitly not the general proof.
